stem: Joseph is a 13-month-old boy brought to the emergency department after his mother found him choking and gagging next to spilled nuts. He is alert, has increased work of breathing with audible stridor and subcostal retractions, is intermittently coughing, and has normal colour. His vital signs are RR 66/min, HR 160/min, BP 88/56, Temp 37.1°C, and SaO2 93% on blow-by oxygen. Which one of the following is the next step in management?

options.text: Immediate direct laryngoscopy with Magills forceps to remove foreign body
Perform a finger sweep of the mouth.

explanation: This is a suspected upper airway foreign body with partial obstruction: the child is breathing, intermittently coughing, and maintaining colour. The next step is urgent senior airway support with ENT/anaesthetic involvement for controlled airway management and possible bronchoscopy. Blind finger sweep is contraindicated, imaging should not delay management, and nebulised adrenaline is for croup rather than foreign body obstruction.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The child has a suspected aspirated/upper airway foreign body with partial obstruction. Because he is still coughing and maintaining colour, the priority is urgent experienced airway support rather than blind removal attempts or delays for imaging.

optionExplanations.A: Direct laryngoscopy and forceps removal may be needed, but only in a controlled setting with senior airway support rather than as the immediate next step from the bedside.
optionExplanations.B: Radiography can assist if the diagnosis is uncertain, but it must not delay definitive management in a child with significant airway symptoms after choking.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. A symptomatic suspected foreign body with partial obstruction requires urgent ENT/anaesthetic review for controlled airway assessment and removal.
optionExplanations.D: Nebulised adrenaline treats upper airway oedema such as croup, not a foreign body aspiration/impaction.
optionExplanations.E: Finger sweep can worsen obstruction and is contraindicated.
